stem: A client with confirmed COPD has a lower post-bronchodilator FEV1 percentage of predicted on repeat spirometry. How should the nurse interpret this value within GOLD spirometric grading?

options.A: A lower FEV1 percentage predicted corresponds to a more severe airflow-obstruction grade.
options.B: A lower FEV1 percentage predicted indicates improved expiratory airflow.
options.C: FEV1 percentage predicted has no role in grading airflow obstruction after COPD is established.
options.D: A lower FEV1 percentage predicted corresponds to a milder airflow-obstruction grade.

rationale: GOLD uses post-bronchodilator FEV1 percentage predicted to grade the severity of airflow obstruction after COPD has been established; lower values correspond to more severe spirometric grades. Overall COPD assessment also considers symptoms and exacerbation risk, so spirometric grade is not the entire clinical severity assessment. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Interpret post-bronchodilator FEV1 percentage predicted as a measure of spirometric airflow-obstruction grade in established COPD.
source_organization: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD)
source_document_title: Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD: 2026 Report
source_locator: Diagnosis and Assessment — classification of severity of airflow obstruction in COPD by post-bronchodilator FEV1 percent predicted
source_claim_supported: In established COPD, lower post-bronchodilator FEV1 percent predicted corresponds to a more severe GOLD spirometric airflow-obstruction grade; broader COPD assessment also includes nonspirometric clinical factors.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — diagnostic testing and interpretation of respiratory function studies
correction_summary: Verified the 2026 GOLD Report is the current strategy document and retained the narrow spirometric-grading claim while explicitly preventing overinterpretation of FEV1 as the entire COPD clinical assessment. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
audit_findings: Current GOLD 2026 materials confirm the current report/pocket guide and the established spirometric framework. The final wording is limited to airflow-obstruction grade and avoids equating FEV1 grade with overall disease burden. Independent second pass passed.
